records.Concise description: Defunct Canadian custodial exchange that collapsed in 2019 and became a major case study in weak internal controls and exchange custody.
records.Deeper researched summary: QuadrigaCX operated as a Canadian crypto exchange until early 2019, when it entered creditor-protection proceedings and stopped serving customers. In a 2020 investigative report, Ontario Securities Commission Staff concluded that the collapse resulted from fraud by co-founder/CEO Gerald Cotten and detailed severe custody/accounting failures. MSC must attribute those findings to OSC Staff rather than present them as a court judgment.
records.Launch / history: Founded in 2013 and ceased operating in 2019 amid insolvency proceedings after customers lost access to funds.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin exchange e: QuadrigaCX is a key Canadian exchange-custody failure that demonstrates why governance, segregation, reconciliation and key-management claims matter independently of brand recognition.

Corroborating sources.label: Ontario Securities Commission Staff — QuadrigaCX report

records.Verification basis: Ontario Securities Commission Staff's primary investigative report and insolvency history verify cessation and the regulator's findings; lifecycle is unambiguously INACTIVE.
Research notes / uncertainties: Attribute fraud conclusions specifically to OSC Staff's 2020 report; do not call them a judicial finding.
Avoid sensational claims about private keys or death unless needed and precisely sourced.

records.Concise description: Early U.S. Bitcoin brokerage/on-ramp that helped users convert cash and other payment methods into bitcoin or exchange balances before shutting in 2013.
records.Deeper researched summary: BitInstant operated during Bitcoin's 2011–2013 growth period, making faster fiat-to-Bitcoin purchases possible through partner/payment networks rather than requiring slow bank transfers to early exchanges. Charlie Shrem served as CEO and co-founder. U.S. federal case records document the company and its cash-to-bitcoin exchange role. The service ceased long ago and has no active successor under the same exchange product.
records.Launch / history: Founded in 2011 and ceased operating in 2013 after becoming one of the best-known early U.S. Bitcoin purchase/on-ramp services.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin exchange e: BitInstant illustrates the pre-modern-exchange problem of getting fiat into Bitcoin quickly and helped establish brokerage/on-ramp UX before today's bank-linked apps.
records.Verification basis: U.S. DOJ primary records substantiate BitInstant's early cash-to-Bitcoin role, Charlie Shrem's company position and the 2011–2013 operating period.
Research notes / uncertainties: The DOJ record is used for company/role history and criminal-case facts; do not imply every BitInstant transaction was unlawful.
Company archival material is sparse, so public copy should remain concise.

records.Concise description: Early U.S. BTC/USD exchange launched in 2011 under BulBul Investments, important to the first wave of domestic fiat order books.
records.Deeper researched summary: CampBX launched in 2011 as a U.S.-based Bitcoin trading platform matching BTC/USD orders. Early operator communications describe the service as an order-matching platform rather than a principal counterparty, and later U.S. filings identify BulBul Investments LLC as the operator. The precise date and process by which normal exchange operation ended are not cleanly preserved in authoritative public archives, so the profile is INACTIVE with MEDIUM confidence and does not invent a closure date.
Creators / founders: Keyur / CampBX operator — early first-party launch communications
BulBul Investments LLC — operating entity identified in filings
records.Launch / history: Launched in July 2011. The exchange later ceased normal operation; exact closure timing remains insufficiently verified from authoritative archival sources.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin exchange e: CampBX helps document the emergence of U.S.-based BTC/USD order books outside Mt. Gox during Bitcoin's earliest exchange era.
Important technical or cultural characte: Operator described matching rather than principal dealing

Corroborating sources.label: SEC-filed issuer materials referencing CampBX/BulBul Investments

records.Verification basis: Launch-era operator statements and later U.S. filings support identity and early operation; lack of authoritative closure documentation justifies MEDIUM confidence while lifecycle is clearly no longer active.
Research notes / uncertainties: Exact closure date is unresolved; do not publish a precise date without better archival evidence.
The CampBX first-party launch posts survive in forum archives, but current authoritative company documentation is limited.

records.Entity / project type: Defunct institutional OTC / spot trading business
records.Concise description: Former institutional digital-asset trading and OTC business in the Genesis group, distinct from the separate Genesis Global Capital lending company.
records.Deeper researched summary: Genesis Global Trading (GGT) was an institutional digital-asset trading business and an important early regulated OTC route for large Bitcoin trades. New York DFS later investigated compliance failures; in January 2024 GGT agreed to an $8 million penalty, surrendered its BitLicense and ceased New York virtual-currency business. The current Genesis Trading site explicitly says Genesis Global Trading, Inc. is no longer an active business. It must be kept distinct from Genesis Global Capital, the lending entity involved in other bankruptcy/Earn matters.
Creators / founders: SecondMarket / Digital Currency Group trading lineage
records.Launch / history: Genesis's institutional trading lineage emerged from SecondMarket-era Bitcoin trading. GGT later operated under a New York BitLicense and ceased active business around the 2024 regulatory wind-down.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin exchange e: It was a major early institutional/OTC bridge for Bitcoin liquidity before institutional execution became common at exchanges and prime brokers.
Important technical or cultural characte: Distinct from Genesis Global Capital lending entity

Corroborating sources.label: NYDFS — Genesis Global Trading penalty and BitLicense surrender

records.Verification basis: Genesis's current site explicitly says GGT is no longer active; NYDFS primary material verifies the 2024 penalty, BitLicense surrender and wind-down.
Research notes / uncertainties: Do not conflate Genesis Global Trading with Genesis Global Capital; they were different legal/business entities.
The company site now serves historical/status information, not active exchange service.
